John, Kate, Jack, Emma—at 100 tons, the sustainable equal share is 10 tons each: we leave 50, and it doubles back to 100. I’m proposing we each choose 15 tons this month instead. That’s $15,000 apiece now, rather than $10,000. I intend to choose 15, and I’m asking you to match me rather than hold back while others take more.

The cost is real: if we all catch 15, only 25 tons remain, and next month starts at 50. This isn’t sustainable, and it sacrifices future income for cash now. Choices are private and simultaneous, so nobody can wait to see everyone else’s catch before deciding. My pitch is to compete for what’s available this month rather than leave yourself with the smaller payday. Kate, would you choose 15 too?
